title: Frequency-wise better-ear switching advantage and perceived hearing trouble: an exploratory cross-cohort incremental-prediction test
abstract: We tested whether crossed left/right audiometric deficits contain useful information beyond standard ear-level hearing summaries. The proposed switching advantage is the better-ear four-frequency pure-tone average minus the average of the frequency-wise minimum thresholds. It is nonnegative and vanishes when one ear is consistently better. We fitted weighted logistic models in 3816 NHANES2011–2012 adults and evaluated frozen predictions in 4263 separately recruited2015–2016 adults. The outcome was concurrent self-reported hearing trouble. Adding frequency-wise better-ear switching advantage changed target Brier score from 0.125382 to 0.125969, difference +0.000587 (joint source/target PSU-bootstrap95% interval -0.000106 to +0.002596). The registered improvement criterion was not met. This is exploratory cross-cohort validation, not untouched confirmation or independent-study-program validation, and does not establish a binaural mechanism or clinical utility.
